verdict: Run the HP UEFI Diagnostics 10.8.6.0 built-in suite on battery power only: Fast Test first, then Extensive Test if clear, then the Component Tests for Power Source, Battery, System Board, and fan — before any BIOS or driver change. Record the failure ID for any failing test.
reasoning: The diagnostic runs entirely outside Windows, so it removes PMF, sensor drivers, graphics driver, and OS power policy as variables in one step — that is the single most discriminating action available between firmware/software and hardware, and it is the only listed option that is non-destructive with no install or flash. The two candidate alternatives both fail their own test: F.11 is security-advisory directed with only 'improved system stability' and no battery or thermal symptom note, so installing it is an update solely because it is newer and it would also destroy the clean pre-change baseline; and the driver route is a dead end because the exact-SKU 25H2 catalogue publishes no PMF, sensor, thermal, or chipset package, while the only graphics package offered is 32.0.22068.0, older than the installed 32.0.31035.1003. The evidence pointing at hardware is specific and battery-path-shaped: lag on roughly 3/5 unplug events and one historical 108 C ACPI thermal event, which is exactly what Power Source, Battery, System Board, and fan component tests are built to adjudicate. UEFI Diagnostics 10.8.6.0 is published exact for board 8DA7, so this is HP's own supported procedure for this machine rather than an improvised step, and a failure ID converts the whole question into an HP support case with evidence.
what_would_change_this: A full clean pass — Fast, Extensive, and all four component tests green — with the lag still reproducible on battery inside the UEFI environment itself would flip this toward firmware, making F.11 the next action. Conversely, an HP advisory or F.11 release note naming battery-only performance, SMU/PMF power limits, or thermal throttling on this exact board would make the flash the discriminating step instead. Also flipping: if the 3/5 lag turns out to be reproducible only under a Windows workload that cannot run in UEFI, the diagnostic cannot observe the symptom and a battery-only Windows counter capture of CPU effective clock and package power would be needed first.
_question: Choose the single best HP-supported next action for a HP OmniBook X Flip 14-fk0xxx with exact SKU BG2S4PA, board ID 8DA7, severe intermittent battery-only lag on about 3/5 unplug events, and one historical ACPI thermal event at 108 C. Current BIOS F.10. HP publishes exact-board BIOS F.11 SP172952 that supersedes F.10, is security-advisory directed, and says only improved system stability, with no battery/thermal symptom note. HP's exact-SKU 25H2 driver catalogue publishes no AMD PMF, AMD sensor, thermal, or general chipset package; its graphics driver 32.0.22068.0 is older than installed 32.0.31035.1003. PMF 26.10.15.0 and AMD UMDF Sensor 1.1.0.37 are signed/started/OK. HP publishes UEFI Diagnostics 10.8.6.0 exact for board 8DA7, and official procedure says start with UEFI Fast Test, then Extensive Test if clear; Component Tests include Power Source, Battery, System Board, and fan diagnostics. Constraints: do not install or flash; do not recommend an update solely because newer; pick one best next action that is safety-aware and most discriminating between firmware/software and hardware.
